chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Al-Rabi', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, by the head of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), there is red clay in which there is healing from every disease except for Al-Sam (death).

He (the narrator) said, 'So we went to the grave after having heard this Hadith, so we dug by the head of the grave. So when we had dug the measurement of a cubit, there appeared to us, from the head of the grave, like red coastal sand the size of a Dirham (coin). So we carried it to Al-Kufa, and we blended it, and went around giving it to the people for them to use it as medication.'

key_terms.الدِّرْهَمُ: A Dirham, a silver coin, used here to describe the size of the clump of clay.
key_terms.السَّامُ: Death (specifically fatal illness or death itself).
key_terms.السِّهْلَةُ: Coastal sand or fine sand, used here to describe the texture/appearance of the clay.
key_terms.تُرْبَةٌ حَمْرَاءُ: Red clay or earth, specifically the substance mentioned in the narration.
key_terms.ذِرَاعٌ: A cubit, a unit of measurement for depth.
key_terms.رَأْسُ الْحُسَيْنِ: The head of Imam Al-Husayn (AS), referring to the specific part of the grave or shrine.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the red clay found near the head of Imam Al-Husayn (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Shia belief in the physical sanctity of Imam Al-Husayn’s grave, specifically identifying the red clay near his head as a source of divine healing (shifa) for all ailments except death (al-sam). The narrators’ journey to retrieve and distribute this clay to Kufa underscores the historical practice of using bodily remains of the Ahl al-Bayt as tangible mediums for spiritual and physical cure.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Yunus Bin Al Rabie, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘By the head of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> there is red clay wherein is a healing from every disease except for the death’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So we went to the grave after having heard this Hadeeth, so we dug by the head of the grave. So when we had dug the measurement of a cubit, there appeared to us, from the head of the grave, like the red coastal sand like the (size of a) Dirham (coin). So we carried it to Al-Kufa, and we blended it, and went around giving it to the people for them to use it as medication’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Ali from Yunus ibn al-Rabi’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that near the head of al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, there is red soil.
It is cure for all kinds of illnesses except al-Sam.

He (the narrator) has said, ‘We then went to the grave after hearing this Hadith. We dug near the head about a yard from the head of the grave and some red sand appeared. It was of the size of a dirham. We took it to al-Kufa and mixed it with other soil. We would give to people who used it as curing medicine.’”
